findings.reason: a worker sent to close on a count "derived from the domain audit's output" would find the audit cannot produce it, and would either add an undeclared field or silently fall back to the census measure the section just replaced.
findings.text: the section says "the family count is derived from the domain audit's output, so one instrument reads physics_domain for both measures", but the audit's row set and `NameDomainState` carry no `physical_base`, and family membership is a census concept (`census_families` groups rows by `n.physical_base`) — so the second done-when item cannot be measured from the instrument the section names without an addition the section does not declare among its deliverables

findings.reason: removing that reading mid-pass leaves §2's before/after and §3's comparison resting on two differently scoped instruments, so the removal needs a declared ordering or dependency rather than a permissive sentence.
findings.text: the new sentence authorises removing "the consistency census's own domain reading", but §2's third done-when item counts with "the same committed instrument" at both ends and §3's second item records the census's divergent-family count beside §2's reading; §5 depends only on `sn-integrity-backlog#s52`, and followup f-scc-001 explicitly lets §2 and §5 run together

findings.reason: names the continuation adds can raise the count past 98 with every §5 repair complete, so the verdict would report the concurrent run rather than this section's work; §2's identical defect was answered by restricting the comparison to a population measured at both ends.
findings.text: the measure requires the family count to be "lower than the consistency census's 2026-11-10 reading of 98", an absolute comparison against a reading taken over 130 families and 3,034 names while §1's lead ruling lets the full-DD continuation run before or beside this pass

response_events.note: §5 no longer claims the family count derives from the audit's output; it states the count of families whose live members carry more than one physics_domain as the endpoint.
